touches.text: Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.

WHY: Law 8: nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and the verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide. A green cannot be self-granted. A machine under CodeMother, not a device: CodeMother does not build, so the tester inside her puts no builder between a build and its verdict, and nothing here needs its own process in the rack, since each proof run is its own process already.

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf. The gates are CodeMother's (9.3.5).

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Either way the system improves. WHY: a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or its implementation, never a conversation about procedure. The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure, and it is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome. Nothing passes a ticket over a red.

A hook registration in .claude/settings.json that a cast ticket's decisions name is approved in advance: it lands at that ticket's BUILDME without a question. WHY: a peer cannot relay Akien's approval of its own hooks, and the ticket is where he already delegated build authority, so the approval names the change, never a messenger. - CC
VERBS: run, notices, CodeMother's verbs reached over the bus (RULE 1). COMMANDS: cairn codemother test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, ...), shortcut cairn test; proofgate (the hook: proofs run by hand).

The seal is checked where the proof runs, not in the command's text: a proof refuses to run outside the tester's seal, so no spelling reaches the live ~/.cairn. proofgate only rewrites the common spelling for convenience. CC's decision, Q#101.

Every sieve carries its own why, and the why names where it came from. Akien designed the inspector tools; CC built each specific sieve from what it read him to mean. So the adjudication in 17.11.6 is against the sieve's own why, done by CC, and never a question to him. The sieves are not perfect and nothing here will be: the whole is always under improvement, and each sieve's why is what lets it be judged. Today build_inspector registers 43 sieves, and the 36 sieves/*.json records carry name, band and dials but no why. The whys live only in docstrings.

A ticket's code is a tool or machine; its life is data. All of its state is on disk, so anyone can instantiate it to talk to it, and any dialog is written to the relevant part of the ticket as it happens. To cross a gate the ticket asks that gate to queue it, sending only its fileref: devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>. The gate instantiates the ticket from that fileref on its own side. A ticket instance then processes the pass or fail: on a pass it goes on to the next step, alerting the probes watching the gate (3.3.4.2); on a fail it asks design to queue it, the same way. Self-queuing is the abstract ticket's (3.3.2), so every kind inherits it and no caller queues a ticket on its behalf. WHY: encapsulation. The ticket crosses as a fileref and the other side builds its own instance, so nothing is shared across the boundary but the address.

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.
